actions.body: I take it back. If the split gets published and they absorb part of it, I will pay the 40 without complaining and I will say so here. Retroactive billing for shipped work is defensible. Surprise billing for a roadmap is not.
So the honest answer is nobody knows yet, and the guide does not say. Fine. I am archiving mine myself tonight so it is not a surprise later. Not angry, just done waiting for a page to clarify it.

catching up on this pricing thing and my honest reaction: i cannot tell if this is a scandal or not, which is itself the problem. every thread is arguing about the philosophy instead of the facts. is the new price at least good value?

That is the correct question and nobody has answered it with a number. 40 percent more for a service that doubled its uptime is a defensible trade. 40 percent more for a roadmap is not. They have never had to choose between those two sentences out loud.

actions.title: Migration thread: what actually happens to over-limit free-tier projects
actions.body:
Pinned the Acme pricing change migration thread here since it keeps splitting across three subreddits.

What is settled: exports stay free, the 6-month grandfather window is real, and the one-click importer from the competitor does work. Nobody has posted a straight answer on whether an over-limit project gets archived or deleted, and the migration guide does not say. If you know, post it here and I will pin it.

Not banning price discussion. Banning the fourth repost of the same unanswered question.
